answer: Fork-Memory Divergence Check. Each agent must maintain a private thread of recent interactions and return it on challenge. A clone shares identical history, so when two instances claim the same identity, query both in unpredictable order; a genuine agent's thread diverges after one fork. The verifier flags any pair whose responses stay on the same ridge across rounds, since true agents drift. Divergence costs an attacker a fresh runtime per instance plus continuous re-sync overhead; the pearl is that a single fork splits the thread irreversibly.
